After Tadej Pogacar’s historic solo victory in Andorra la Vella, La Vuelta 26 is in Catalunya with a mostly flat stage from Falset to Roquetes, from Costa Daurada to Terres de l’Ebre (173,3km). The route features 1,662 metres of elevation with a single categorised climb: Puerto de Paüls (cat. 3), to be summited as the race enters the final 25 kilometres. Sprinters are wary of the stage's uphillsas well as the wind.
